headline: Planning Commission splits recommendations on hotel rezoning bills

meeting.summary: Planning Commission splits recommendations on hotel rezoning bills.
meeting.recap: Bill 9 ends vacation rentals in apartment districts by December 31, 2028, in West Maui and December 31, 2030, elsewhere.[[0:06:09]] The commission reviewed two council resolutions to rezone specific properties into new H3 and H4 hotel districts.[[0:13:08]] The bills cover about 48 properties and a little over 3,400 units.[[0:13:29]] Staff said their sole purpose is to let these properties keep vacation rentals.[[0:14:27]] The commission must report to the council by November 24, 2026.[[0:16:23]] The Office of Hawaiian Affairs opposed both resolutions.[[0:51:07]] The president of the Maui Sunset timeshare association supported hotel zoning for that property.[[1:20:43]] A Lahaina Community Land Trust staff member urged returning non-hotel units to housing.[[2:37:48]] A commissioner said the commission lacked enough information to evaluate the properties.[[5:21:44]] A friendly amendment added a hotel-like property in Hāna for approval.[[7:46:51]] The final motion recommends approving the two variance and two all-timeshare properties.[[7:54:27]] It recommends denial for single-owner, mixed timeshare, leasehold and hotel-like properties.[[7:54:43]] A separate motion asked the council to explore using public funds for housing.[[8:10:44]] The main motion passed with five yes votes, including one abstention, and one no.[[8:15:08]]
decided: A commissioner's proposal to require certified shoreline surveys for shoreline properties did not get a second.
The commission voted to ask the council to explore using public funds for housing.
The commission voted to recommend approval for the variance, all-timeshare and one Hāna property, and denial for the other property groups.
meeting.next: Staff will take a report back to the council, which will decide on the bills at a future meeting. Staff said he will transfer the motion information to the council.
